title: Psychic Practice, Step by Step
subtitle: A Workbook for Beginners, from First Hunch to Trusted Insight
author: Maren Ashby
topic: A step-by-step practice workbook for developing intuition and psychic perception from zero, set inside a spiritual frame. Each section opens with a few warm paragraphs on why and how. The rest of the section is work on the page: guided exercises, scored test sheets, logs, self-profiles and reflection prompts.
audience: Adults who are open to intuition and to the spiritual side of life, and who have already had experiences they can't explain: a hunch that turned out right, a dream that came true, knowing who was calling before the phone rang. Most are complete beginners. They may have read an introduction or two, but they still don't know what to do, in what order, or how to tell whether it's working. They want a calm, safe, structured practice they can do alone at home in short sessions, pen in hand. Some have more experience: they already meditate, work with energy or give readings, and they want a disciplined routine and an honest record of their practice. None of them is looking for proof that psychic ability exists, or for a skeptical debate.
promise: A practice the reader does, not one they only read about. Section by section the book takes them from noticing their first hunches to working with impressions they have learned to check. Along the way they get: a short opening and closing routine to stay grounded and protected; ways to tell intuition from anxiety or wishful thinking; a profile of their strongest intuitive sense, with exercises for each sense; low-stakes experiments scored on the page; a symbol dictionary built from their own impressions; logs for signs and dreams; partner exercises with an ethical framework; a guided meditation to meet a guide; and, at the end, a routine they design themselves. Every page asks for something different. The book promises a method and a record of the reader's own progress. It does not promise psychic powers, accuracy or results.
tone: Warm, close and plain-spoken, like an experienced friend coaching at the kitchen table. Explanations are short, steps are numbered and clear, and encouragement comes without hype. The book takes the spiritual frame seriously (energy, guides, meditation) and respects the reader's pace. It never suggests the reader has to be or do more than they are. It is honest about misses, never frightening about spirits or energy, and makes no guarantees.
